item: Semi-Markov fitting constants fixed before any out-of-sample run
detail: Expectation-maximisation: at most 30 iterations; stop when the training log-likelihood improves by less than 0.01; variance floor 0.001 on scaled features; negative binomial r bounded to 0.05-200 and p to 0.0001-0.9999; each of the five starts is the plain HMM fitted with that seed, rewritten with geometric durations. These were not in the frozen settings table because the model had not been specified at that level; they are fixed here and will not be changed after the out-of-sample run.

Geometric durations reproduce the plain forward filter to 1e-10; hazard of a geometric law is constant and the cap forces an exit; filter unchanged by truncation; on simulated data with mean regime lengths 41 and 21 days the fit recovers 39.2 and 20.7, with r well above 1 and a higher likelihood than the plain HMM it started from; likelihood never decreases across iterations; filtered regime classification on held-out simulated data at least as accurate as the plain HMM. Walk-forward look-ahead test passed at 3 cuts over the first two blocks. Signals were compared for equality only; no performance was computed.

item: Decoding, survival, backtest, bootstrap and evaluation tests
detail: Plain most-likely path equals hmmlearn's; semi-Markov path with geometric durations equals the plain one and recovers simulated regimes on over 97% of days; Kaplan-Meier matches a textbook censored case; a signal first affects the return two days later; cost equals turnover times the rate; cash trades are free; weights drift between trades; the band blocks a 3-point change and allows a 6-point one; monthly rule trades once a month; metrics match hand calculations; bootstrap mean block length about 21 days, reproducible, exactly zero for identical series; evaluation runs end to end on a made-up panel; benchmark signals pass the look-ahead test.
outcome: 39 fast tests passed; 2 slow look-ahead tests passed earlier

item: Evaluation choices fixed before the out-of-sample run
detail: (a) All strategies start in cash on 2015-01-01, receive their first signal that day, trade at the next close and are measured from the third out-of-sample day. (b) The rebalancing band compares the target equity weight with the held (drifted) equity weight; on a trade all three weights are set to target. (c) Turnover is the absolute change in the equity weight plus the absolute change in the gold weight; cash moves are free; the cost of a trade is taken from the capital earning the next day's return. (d) Results are reported at 10 basis points (main), 0 (before costs) and 25 (sensitivity). (e) Sub-periods: 2015-2019, 2020, 2021-2026. (f) Sharpe differences are bootstrapped for each model strategy against each of the four benchmarks, and for the semi-Markov strategy against the plain HMM strategy: 9 comparisons per cost level.
